name: Tobiah
overview: Tobiah was a male Ammonite official known for his opposition to Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. His role as an adversary highlights the challenges faced by God's people during this period. Scripture identifies him specifically as an Ammonite, emphasizing his foreign origin and opposition to the Jewish community.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Tobiah' means 'YHWH is good,' reflecting a Hebrew theophoric element despite Tobiah being an Ammonite. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 2:10, underscores the common use of the divine name in personal names of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Tobiah was the son-in-law of Shecaniah, as stated in Nehemiah 6:18. Beyond this connection, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tobiah's significance lies in his active opposition to Nehemiah's leadership and the restoration efforts in Jerusalem. As an Ammonite official, he represents the external resistance faced by the returned exiles striving to rebuild both the city and their community under God's guidance. His opposition serves as a narrative example of spiritual and political challenges encountered in fulfilling God's purposes.
